target_customer: Consumers with personal 3D printers and designers who wanted to sell printable designs
problem: People with a home 3D printer had no easy marketplace for finding, buying and printing good designs, and designers had no storefront to sell to them.
business_model: marketplace for printable 3D designs with a one-click single print option
product_category: 3D printing design marketplace and print software

founders.name: Jon Miller Schwartz
founders.background_notes: The YC page lists Arena AI, Voodoo Manufacturing (YC W17) and Body Labs, which are all after Layer By Layer. The idea came out of studying for an engineering final with Max Friefeld (HMC article).

founders.name: Max Friefeld
education: Harvey Mudd College, Computer and Electrical Engineering, 2013
founders.background_notes: Later co-founded Voodoo Manufacturing and worked at Boston Consulting Group per the YC page.

founders.name: Oliver Ortlieb
education: Harvey Mudd College, BS Computer Science
founders.background_notes: The student newspaper spells the surname Orlieb and gives class of 2012. The YC page says he holds several 3D printing patents.

technical_complexity.rationale: A marketplace plus a streaming print pipeline for printer hardware that was changing quickly. MakerBot later deployed the streaming technology in its digital store and for rights management of printable files.

defensibility.rationale: Marketplaces for designs already existed and the print-direct feature could be copied by the printer makers themselves, which is what the acquirer did by absorbing the team.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: MakerBot, the printer vendor that also ran Thingiverse, bought the company in November 2014 and moved the team to its Brooklyn office.

market_need_then: Consumer 3D printers were just reaching home users in 2013, and a student article describes no Amazon or iTunes style store existing for designers to sell to people with their own printers.

branding.domain_note: Used layerbylayer.com; the domain now redirects to a GoDaddy for-sale page.
branding.brand_signature: InstaPrint, the one-click Print button for a single model (feature, not a brand asset)
branding.community_and_virality: Named to the Kairos 50 list of top student founded companies per Harvey Mudd coverage. No sign of a fan community.

brand_strength.rationale: Small student startup with a name that describes the production method. The only press found is launch and acquisition coverage.

outcome_analysis: Two Harvey Mudd seniors and an alumnus built a marketplace and print-direct tool for the early consumer 3D printer market. Rather than raise venture rounds that could be found, the small team was bought by MakerBot in November 2014 to build user-friendly software and a digital store for its ecosystem, which reads as a product and talent acquisition by the leading printer vendor.
notes: The YC page and directory say acquired in February 2014; MakerBot's own press release and trade coverage date it to 13 November 2014, which is used here. Funding search found only a Crunchbase profile with no readable figures, so no rounds are recorded. No dated competitor source for 2013 was found: the search surfaced later alternatives lists only, so the list is empty. Deal price not disclosed.
